### Start MCP Inspector

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Command to start the MCP Inspector using npx, which is used to interact with MCP-compatible services.

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
```

### Start TrendRadar Services with Docker Compose

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This set of commands demonstrates how to start the TrendRadar services using Docker Compose. It includes pulling the latest images and starting all services, or specific services like the news push or AI analysis components.

```bash
# Pull latest images
docker compose pull

# Start all services (trendradar + trendradar-mcp)
docker compose up -d
```

```bash
# Start trendradar only (scheduled crawling and push)
docker compose pull trendradar
docker compose up -d trendradar
```

```bash
# Start trendradar-mcp only (AI analysis interface)
docker compose pull trendradar-mcp
docker compose up -d trendradar-mcp
```

--------------------------------

### Build and Start TrendRadar Services Locally

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This section provides instructions for developers who need to build the TrendRadar project from source. It covers cloning the repository, modifying configuration files, and then building and starting the services using Docker Compose.

```bash
# Clone project
git clone https://github.com/sansan0/TrendRadar.git
cd TrendRadar

# Modify config files
vim config/config.yaml
vim config/frequency_words.txt

# Use build version docker compose
cd docker
cp docker-compose-build.yml docker-compose.yml
```

```bash
# Option A: Build and start all services
docker compose build
docker compose up -d

# Option B: Build and start news push service only
docker compose build trendradar
docker compose up -d trendradar
```

--------------------------------

### Download Docker Compose Separately and Configure

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This method allows for a more manual setup by downloading the docker-compose.yml and .env files separately. It requires creating directories for configuration and output, downloading config files, and modifying volume paths in the docker-compose.yml before running.

```bash
mkdir trendradar && cd trendradar
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sansan0/TrendRadar/master/docker/docker-compose.yml
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sansan0/TrendRadar/master/docker/.env
mkdir -p config output
# Download config files
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sansan0/TrendRadar/master/config/config.yaml -P config/
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sansan0/TrendRadar/master/config/frequency_words.txt -P config/
# Modify volume paths in docker-compose.yml: ../config -> ./config, ../output -> ./output
docker compose up -d
```

--------------------------------

### Start MCP Service Separately (Linux/Mac)

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This command starts the MCP (Message Communication Protocol) service as a detached Docker container on Linux or macOS. It maps local configuration and output directories into the container and sets the timezone.

```bash
# Linux/Mac
docker run -d --name trendradar-mcp \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3333:3333 \
  -v $(pwd)/config:/app/config:ro \
  -v $(pwd)/output:/app/output:ro \
  -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  wantcat/trendradar-mcp:latest
```

### Configuration Strategy Example

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Illustrates a step-by-step approach to refining keyword configurations from broad to strict. It shows how to add required and filter words incrementally to achieve more precise matching, avoiding over-complexity by splitting large groups into smaller, focused ones.

```text
# Step 1: Start with broad keywords for testing
Artificial Intelligence
AI
ChatGPT

# Step 2: After finding mismatches, add required words
Artificial Intelligence
AI
ChatGPT
+technology

# Step 3: After finding noise, add filter words
Artificial Intelligence
AI
ChatGPT
+technology
!advertisement
!training
```

```text
# Recommended: Split into precise groups
Huawei
OPPO
+new product

Apple
Samsung
+launch

phone
sales
+market
```

### Combined Configuration Example

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Presents a combined `config.yaml` file that sets both the keyword sorting priority and the global maximum news count per keyword. This configuration ensures that results are sorted by config position first and limits the number of items shown per keyword.

```yaml
# config.yaml
report:
  sort_by_position_first: true   # Config order priority
  max_news_per_keyword: 10       # Global default max 10 per keyword
```

### Keyword-Specific Display Count Example

Tesla

### Configure Cursor with TrendRadar MCP (JSON)

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Configuration examples for integrating TrendRadar MCP with the Cursor editor. Supports both HTTP and STDIO modes. STDIO mode is recommended for its one-time configuration.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "trendradar": {
      "url": "http://localhost:3333/mcp",
      "description": "TrendRadar News Trending Aggregation Analysis"
    }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "trendradar": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": [
        "--directory",
        "/path/to/TrendRadar",
        "run",
        "python",
        "-m",
        "mcp_server.server"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```

### Configure Push Time Window with Docker Environment Variables

### Configure Custom Monitoring Platforms (YAML)

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet shows how to enable and configure custom news monitoring platforms within the TrendRadar application. It specifies the 'platforms' section in 'config/config.yaml' and lists example sources like Toutiao and Baidu.

```yaml
platforms:
  enabled: true                       # Enable trending platform crawling
  sources:
    - id: "toutiao"
      name: "Toutiao"
    - id: "baidu"
      name: "Baidu Hot Search"
    - id: "wallstreetcn-hot"
      name: "Wallstreetcn"
    # Add more platforms...

```

--------------------------------

### Configure Push Time Window in YAML

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Control when push notifications are sent by configuring the `notification.push_window` section in `config/config.yaml`. You can enable or disable the time window, set the start and end times (in Beijing time), and specify if pushes should occur only once per day within that window.

```yaml
notification:
  push_window:
    enabled: false                    # Whether to enable
    start: "20:00"                    # Start time (Beijing time)
    end: "22:00"                      # End time (Beijing time)
    once_per_day: true                # Push only once per day
```

```yaml
notification:
  push_window:
    enabled: true
    start: "20:00"
    end: "22:00"
    once_per_day: true
```

```yaml
notification:
  push_window:
    enabled: true
    start: "09:00"
    end: "18:00"
    once_per_day: false
```

```text
Settings → MCP Server → Add
Type: streamableHttp
URL: http://127.0.0.1:3333/mcp
```

### TrendRadar HTTP Service

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Information on starting the TrendRadar HTTP service and connecting to it via a browser.

```APIDOC
## TrendRadar HTTP Service

### Description

This section details how to start the TrendRadar HTTP service and access its functionalities through a web browser. It also lists the available tools and their respective functions.

### Method

N/A (Service Start)

### Endpoint

`http://localhost:3333/mcp`

### Parameters

N/A

### Request Example

N/A

### Response

#### Success Response (200)

- **Ping Server**: Verifies server connection.
- **List Tools**: Returns a list of available tools:
  - **Date Parsing**: `resolve_date_range`
  - **Basic Query**: `get_latest_news`, `get_news_by_date`, `get_trending_topics`
  - **Smart Search**: `search_news`, `search_related_news_history`
  - **Advanced Analysis**: `analyze_topic_trend`, `analyze_data_insights`, `analyze_sentiment`, `find_similar_news`, `generate_summary_report`
  - **System Management**: `get_current_config`, `get_system_status`, `trigger_crawl`

#### Response Example

```json
{
  "tools": [
    "resolve_date_range",
    "get_latest_news",
    "get_news_by_date",
    "get_trending_topics",
    "search_news",
    "search_related_news_history",
    "analyze_topic_trend",
    "analyze_data_insights",
    "analyze_sentiment",
    "find_similar_news",
    "generate_summary_report",
    "get_current_config",
    "get_system_status",
    "trigger_crawl"
  ]
}
```
```

### Configure Timezone Settings

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Adjust the timezone for push notifications to match your local time. The configuration is located in `config/config.yaml`. Examples for Los Angeles and London are provided.

```yaml
app:
  timezone: "Asia/Shanghai"  # Default is China Standard Time
```

### Configure Multi-Platform Notifications (YAML)

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet demonstrates how to configure the `notification` section in `config/config.yaml` to send alerts to multiple platforms. It shows how to separate multiple URLs or tokens with a semicolon ';'. Sensitive information like passwords or tokens should not be directly written in this file but managed via GitHub Secrets or .env files.

```yaml
notification:
  feishu_webhook_url: "https://hook1...;https://hook2...;https://hook3..."
  dingtalk_webhook_url: "https://oapi...;https://oapi..."
  telegram_bot_token: "tokenA;tokenB"
  telegram_chat_id: "userA;userB"
  ntfy_topic: "topic1;topic2;topic3"
  ntfy_token: "token1;;token3"

```

### Set Auto-Run Frequency in GitHub Actions Workflow

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Configure the auto-run frequency of the crawler in GitHub Actions by defining a cron schedule in the `.github/workflows/crawler.yml` file. The example provided sets the crawler to run every hour.

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 * * * *"  # Run every hour
```

### Deploy ntfy Server using Docker

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet shows how to deploy an ntfy notification server using Docker. It maps port 80 and mounts a volume for cache persistence. This is useful for users who want to self-host ntfy for complete privacy control.

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name ntfy \
  -p 80:80 \
  -v /var/cache/ntfy:/var/cache/ntfy \
  binwiederhier/ntfy \
  serve --cache-file /var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Hotness Algorithm Weights in YAML

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet shows how to adjust the weights for ranking, frequency, and hotness in the `config/config.yaml` file to customize the hotness algorithm. The weights must sum to 1.0. Adjustments should be made incrementally (0.1-0.2) to observe effects.

```yaml
advanced:
  weight:
    rank: 0.6           # Ranking weight
    frequency: 0.3      # Frequency weight
    hotness: 0.1        # Hotness weight
```

```yaml
advanced:
  weight:
    rank: 0.8           # Mainly focus on ranking
    frequency: 0.1      # Less concern about continuity
    hotness: 0.1
```

```yaml
advanced:
  weight:
    rank: 0.4           # Moderate ranking focus
    frequency: 0.5      # Emphasize sustained heat within the day
    hotness: 0.1
```

### Download TrendRadar Configuration Files using Wget

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet shows how to download essential configuration files for TrendRadar using wget. It includes configuration files for the application, frequency words, AI analysis prompts, and Docker environment variables.

# Create directory structure
mkdir -p trendradar/{config,docker}

# Download docker compose config

### Custom Display Names with Regex

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Allows setting custom display names for regex patterns to improve readability in push notifications and HTML pages. The syntax is `/pattern/ => Display Name`. Flags in the pattern are ignored as case-insensitivity is always enabled.

```txt
/(?<![a-zA-Z])ai(?![a-zA-Z])/ => AI Related
artificial intelligence
```

```txt
# Config
/(?<![a-zA-Z])ai(?![a-zA-Z])/ => AI Related
artificial intelligence
```

### Global Display Count Limit Configuration

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Demonstrates how to set a global limit for the number of news items displayed per keyword using `max_news_per_keyword` in `config.yaml`. A value of 0 means unlimited. This setting can be overridden by specific keyword configurations.

```yaml
report:
  max_news_per_keyword: 10  # Max 10 per keyword (0=unlimited)
```

### Enable HTML Report Generation in config.yaml

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This YAML snippet demonstrates how to enable HTML report generation, a prerequisite for the Email Push functionality. Ensure `storage.formats.html` is set to `true` to avoid errors related to missing HTML files.

```yaml
storage:
  formats:
    sqlite: true
    txt: false
    html: true   # Must be enabled, otherwise email push will fail
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize and Run NewsAnalyzer (Python)

Source: https://context7.com/sansan0/trendradar/llms.txt

Initializes the NewsAnalyzer class, which orchestrates the news crawling, analysis, and notification pipeline. Can be initialized with default configuration or a custom configuration object, and then executed using the run() method.

```python
from trendradar.__main__ import NewsAnalyzer
from trendradar.core import load_config

# Initialize with default config
analyzer = NewsAnalyzer()

# Or with custom config
config = load_config()
config['REPORT_MODE'] = 'incremental'  # Options: incremental, current, daily
analyzer = NewsAnalyzer(config=config)

# Run the complete analysis pipeline
analyzer.run()
```

--------------------------------

### Get Trending Topics Statistics with DataQueryTools (Python)

Source: https://context7.com/sansan0/trendradar/llms.txt

Analyze and retrieve trending topic statistics using `DataQueryTools`. This function supports different modes ('current', 'daily') and extraction methods ('keywords', 'auto_extract') for identifying hot topics.

```python
from mcp_server.tools.data_query import DataQueryTools

tools = DataQueryTools()

# Get top 10 trending topics using preset keywords
result = tools.get_trending_topics(
    top_n=10,
    mode="current",      # "current" or "daily"
    extract_mode="keywords"  # "keywords" or "auto_extract"
)

# Auto-extract high-frequency words from titles
result = tools.get_trending_topics(
    top_n=20,
    mode="daily",
    extract_mode="auto_extract"
)

# Example response:
# {
#     "success": True,
#     "topics": [
#         {"keyword": "人工智能", "frequency": 45, "matched_news": 38, "trend": "stable"},
#         {"keyword": "特斯拉", "frequency": 32, "matched_news": 28, "trend": "rising"}
#     ],
#     "mode": "daily",
#     "extract_mode": "keywords"
# }
```

--------------------------------

### Check Port Occupancy

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Commands to check if a specific port (e.g., 3333) is already in use on Windows or Mac/Linux systems.

```bash
# Windows
netstat -ano | findstr :3333
```

```bash
# Mac/Linux
lsof -i :3333
```

--------------------------------

### Build Docker Images for Specific Architecture

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Builds Docker images for a specified architecture (e.g., arm64). By default, it builds amd64 images. Set the DOCKER_ARCH environment variable to change the target architecture.

```bash
export DOCKER_ARCH=arm64
docker compose build
```

--------------------------------

### Keyword Sorting Priority Configuration

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Shows how to configure keyword sorting priority in the `config.yaml` file. Setting `sort_by_position_first` to `true` prioritizes configuration order, while `false` (default) prioritizes news count. This affects how results are displayed when multiple keywords match.

```yaml
report:
  sort_by_position_first: false  # Sorting priority config
```

```yaml
report:
  sort_by_position_first: true   # Config order priority
```

--------------------------------

### Configure VSCode Continue with TrendRadar MCP (JSON)

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

Configuration for VSCode's Continue extension to integrate with TrendRadar MCP using the STDIO transport method. This allows for smart analysis directly within the VSCode environment.

```json
{
  "experimental": {
    "modelContextProtocolServers": [
      {
        "transport": {
          "type": "stdio",
          "command": "uv",
          "args": [
            "--directory",
            "/path/to/TrendRadar",
            "run",
            "python",
            "-m",
            "mcp_server.server"
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy Bark Server using Docker

Source: https://github.com/sansan0/trendradar/blob/master/README-EN.md

This snippet demonstrates deploying a Bark notification server using Docker. It maps port 8080 and is suitable for users seeking complete privacy control for iOS notifications.

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name bark-server \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  finab/bark-server
```
